turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes, so let's start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
I asked you a question first, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in? Answer that, and then show me whatever you've brought.
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
I haven't said anything about a timestamp, Hale. What timestamp, and who decided on the zero?
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to flag it." Under which section of your own procedure, Hale? And you still haven't told me who decided, or whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
